title: The Sun and the Ambassador: Daily Mysteries of Light and Darkness
description: A triple chapter on the sun as visible icon of the Divine. (T66) The sun fashioned to the likeness of the First Greatness, performing seven goods of light against night's seven wickednesses. (T67) The sun and night as the two visible mysteries by which heaven and hell are made daily legible — five works of the sun (light, beauty, peace, releasing the Living Soul, power-and-taste) and three exaltations corresponding to the Father. (T68) The Ambassador in the sun: sunrise as the standing image of the First Man's primal shining that drove the sons of Darkness from their storehouses, and sunset as the consummating Extraction in which the last Andrias gathers all light into the Pleroma while Death is shut into the sunless night.
